A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NUCLR work, with matching authors, objectives, algorithms, and experiments. The complete documents, including Appendices A-G, contain sufficient readable text, equations, tables, and figures for reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 3.3 reports original synthetic experiments; Section 4 and Appendix G report original CC3M/CC12M pretraining evaluations, ablations, and popularity analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains the original empirical results and adds classification evaluations on ImageNet-R, DTD, and Food-101, plus an expanded synthetic experiment.

M1.justification: The popularity optimization, alternating model/popularity updates, moving-average estimators, and positive-pair adjustment remain unchanged in Section 3.4 and Algorithm 1. Notation corrections and expanded computational explanations do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: V2 substantially expands classification coverage beyond CIFAR100 and ImageNet1k by adding ImageNet-R, texture recognition on DTD, and food recognition on Food-101. CC3M/CC12M pretraining and the retrieval datasets remain. The synthetic study also adds a less skewed data-generating distribution.

E2.justification: CLIP, DCL, SigLIP, CyCLIP, and SogCLR remain the main comparators, and the appendix retains iSogCLR. The new benchmarks use the existing comparator set. SigLIP's omission from the prose preceding Table 2 does not remove an evaluated comparator: it was never a row in that table.

E3.justification: The existing architectures, batch size, training duration, and task metrics remain unchanged. Appendix G.2 adds a controlled comparison of data-generating temperatures 0.2 and 1.0 and KDE popularity plots at n=100. Table 1's overall mean now aggregates five benchmarks instead of four.

E4.justification: Figure 6 extends the toy analysis to test how popularity-distribution skew affects generalization and approximation errors. V1's real-data histograms of learned zeta and their analysis are removed from Appendix G. The component ablations, initialization comparison, and qualitative image examples are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three runs with different random seeds and retain per-dataset uncertainty values. V2 removes the ± uncertainty values from Table 1's aggregate Mean column; corresponding uncertainty reporting remains in Tables 2 and 3. No increase in run counts is reported.

E6.justification: Substantial new results accompany the expanded evaluations. Table 1 adds ImageNet-R scores: NUCLR obtains 43.82/55.24 versus SogCLR's 42.65/54.54 after CC3M/CC12M training. Table 4 adds DTD/Food-101 results, including a CC3M Food-101 exception where NUCLR trails SogCLR, 22.22 versus 22.33. Original per-dataset scores in Tables 1-3 remain unchanged. Figure 6 expands the synthetic findings, while the learned-zeta histogram results disappear.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 corrects the error-term exponent from E_w(x_i,y_i) to E_w(x_i,y_j), matching Appendix D. Proposition 1's density condition and variance derivation are revised. Appendix F.1 replaces the O(B) additional-cost assertion with an O(B²) derivation. V1's formal asymptotic-InfoNCE comparison is removed, while the main theoretical framework and Theorem 2 remain.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: MIS connects DPM to contrastive learning, uniform popularity approximation incurs persistent error, nonparametric optimization motivates NUCLR, and NUCLR achieves superior overall downstream performance. The new infinite discriminative learning terminology does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4 shifts emphasis from marginal ImageNet1k gains to larger gains on the harder ImageNet-R benchmark. V2 removes the explicit argument questioning asymptotic InfoNCE's conditional-density interpretation and the interpretation of real-data popularity histograms. The conclusion's memory limitation and open questions about generation and predicting popularity remain.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-availability statement and repository address, discloses that the model exceeds 70 million parameters, and explains reuse of forward computations in Appendix F.1. It also states that the five-epoch warm-up duration was not tuned. Existing synthetic sampling details are relocated to Appendix G.1 rather than newly introduced.

R1.justification: New Appendix A.3 relates NUCLR to long-tailed contrastive learning, including Assran et al. (2023b), Zhou et al. (2023b), and the already-cited Qiu et al. Remark 3 adds connections to empirical X-risk minimization and FCCO, with supporting citations. New dataset references are also added; the broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Local rewrites clarify data prediction, introduce infinite discriminative learning terminology, and explain the root-finding motivation. The toy setup moves from Section 3.3 to Appendix G.1, and Appendix G is reorganized. A conference header and acknowledgments are added, but the main narrative and section structure remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains an ImageNet-R column and grouped task headers. Figure 6 becomes a six-panel display, Table 4 is added, and the learned-zeta histogram figure is removed. Retained image examples are renumbered and resized, with some appendix tables relocated. The overall visual format remains stable.

improvement.justification: The additional classification domains and controlled distribution-skew experiment strengthen empirical support for the unchanged method. The corrected theorem index, revised cost accounting, and code-access information improve precision and reproducibility. These gains outweigh the loss of the real-data popularity histograms and aggregate uncertainty in Table 1, but constitute a limited refinement of an already developed paper.
